newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks sink one pct after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks sink one pct after rate hike.

text.p: Toronto stocks sank almost one percent on Thursday after the Bank of Canada hiked short-term interest rates by 25 basis points, prompting investors to sell stocks in favor of the dollar.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 61.41 points to end at 6453.65. Trading was heavy at 96 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 bilion).
"Rates up a quarter (point) is enough to give a record high market sometimes needed doses of reality," said Yorkton Securities institutional equities trader Pier Donnini.
In a surprise move on Thursday, Canada's central bank boosted its influential bank rate to 3.5 percent, the first such hike in more than two years.

Katherine Beattie, MMS International analyst, said that higher interest rates provided competition for stocks as market players snapped up fixed-income instruments, betting that rates would go higher.
All of Toronto's 14 sectors dropped except for conglomerates. The transportation group shed the most points, followed by industrial products and interest-sensitive utilities.
Declining stocks beat out advancers 591 to 416, while 276 finished steady.

In individual issues, Moore Corp Ltd. fell 2.25 to 27.80 in trading of almost 2.5 million shares. The business forms maker said late on Wednesday that second-quarter and full-year earnings would underperform analysts' estimates.
Banks were also hit by the rate hike, with Royal Bank of Canada -- Canada's biggest -- down 0.55 to 62.55 in heavy trading.
Business software company Cognos Inc. fell 3 to 44 in light trading. Late on Wednesday it reported lower first-quarter profits after a writedown.
